test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

My friend told me that he was very thirsty and requested me to give him a glass of water.

options.text: My friend was saying to me, "I am very thirsty. Please give me a glass of water."
My friend told to me, "I am very thirsty. Please give me a glass of water."
My friend said to me, "I was very thirsty. Gave me a glass of water."
My friend said to me, "I am very thirsty. Please give me a glass of water."

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reported sentence is "My friend told me that he was very thirsty and requested me to give him a glass of water."
 
• The corresponding direct speech would be "My friend said to me, 'I am very thirsty. Please give me a glass of water.'"
 
• This maintains the present tense of 'am' (matching the 'is' in the indirect speech) and adds a polite request 'Please give me a glass of water'.

Therefore, the correct answer is - **Option 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Options 1, 2, and 3 present incorrect structures of this sentence.
 
• **In option 1**, 'was saying' suggests an ongoing past action, which isn't implied in the original sentence. 
 
• **In option 2**, 'told to me' is incorrect as 'told' should be followed directly by the object without the preposition 'to'. 
 
• **In option 3,** the usage of 'was' instead of 'am' and 'gave' instead of 'give' results in an inconsistent tense.
